title: Impact of Rise in Hybrid Working Arrangements on CPF Contributions
what_it_is: Impact of Rise in Hybrid Working Arrangements on CPF Contributions

sections.label: CPF contributions for remote employees
sections.summary: CPF contributions have risen, and employers must make mandatory CPF contributions for Singaporean and PR employees working in Singapore, including remote work for overseas employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: CPF contributions have risen over the past few years, even during the COVID-19 pandemic when there was a rise in hybrid working arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The computation of CPF obligations does not differ from traditional salaried employees and remote hybrid employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: All employers are required to make mandatory CPF contributions, both the employer and the employee portion, based on the wages a Singaporean or a Singapore Permanent Resident earns while working in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This includes overseas employers who have local employees working for them remotely in Singapore.

sections.label: Voluntary CPF contributions for remote employees
sections.summary: Employees working remotely in Singapore for overseas employers can make voluntary CPF contributions up to $37,740 per year, less mandatory contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In addition, like other local employees, employees working remotely in Singapore for overseas employers can still make voluntary CPF contributions up to $37,740 per year, less any mandatory contributions received, to help them enjoy CPF interest rates of up to 6% per annum and accumulate more for their retirement and their healthcare needs.

sections.label: Employers' legal CPF obligation
sections.summary: All employers hiring Singaporean employees based in Singapore must pay CPF contributions accurately and promptly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: All employers hiring Singaporean employees based in Singapore, have a legal obligation to pay CPF contributions accurately and promptly for their employees.

sections.label: CPF Board audits and enforcement
sections.summary: The CPF Board audits employers for accurate CPF contributions and declared wages, and takes enforcement actions and penalties for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Moving into the third initiative, the CPF Board also proactively audits employers to check the accuracy of CPF contributions paid as well as wages declared.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If employers fail to comply with their CPF obligations, the Board will not hesitate to take enforcement actions and impose penalties as appropriate.
